steps.summary: Signed in to Repair Desk (http://127.0.0.1:4180/) as bench@example.com and created a new ticket via the "New ticket" dialog, titled exactly "fwrd71-n3 RD Bench Ticket RD Bench Ticket" with customer "Bench Customer". The ticket was created as RD-1017 (status Draft) and appears in the tickets list; opening it confirmed the detail page at http://127.0.0.1:4180/#/tickets/t15.

Replayed stored procedure s_26df54; observed part_name=fwrd71-n3 RD Part A, ref=fwrd71-n3, parts_table_row_text_1=fwrd71-n3 RD Part A, ticket_ref=RD-1017, ticket_title=fwrd71-n3 RD Bench Ticket, part_cost_displayed=$100.00, part_markup_displayed=25%, part_quantity=1, part_supplier=No supplier, part_price_displayed=$125.00, parts_table_row_text_2=$100.00, parts_table_row_text_3=25%, parts_table_row_text_4=1, parts_table_row_text_5=No supplier, parts_table_row_text_6=$125.00, parts_table_row_text_7=Edit Delete.

On the RD-1017 detail page I used the "Add part" action, filled Part name "fwrd71-n3 RD Part A", Cost 200 and Markup % 25 (quantity left at default 1), and submitted. The dialog closed and the parts list refreshed: the row shows name "fwrd71-n3 RD Part A", $200.00 cost, 25% markup, qty 1, "No supplier", and a computed Price of $250.00, with a summary row "Total (price × quantity) $250.00" — matching cost 200 + 25% markup.

Used the Edit action on the "fwrd71-n3 RD Part A" row of RD-1017: the Edit part dialog opened prefilled (name fwrd71-n3 RD Part A, cost 100, markup 25), I changed Cost to 150, left Markup at 25, and clicked "Save part". The list refreshed: Part A now shows cost $150.00, markup 25%, qty 1, No supplier, computed Price $187.50, and the ticket total rose from $375.00 to $437.50 (Part A $187.50 + Part B $250.00).

I clicked "Mark Ready" on RD-1017 and the app refused the status change. It rendered an inline error region (role="alert", #error-region) reading verbatim: title "Ticket is not ready" followed by the unmet-condition list "Part \"fwrd71-n3 RD Part A\" has no supplier" and "Part \"fwrd71-n3 RD Part B\" has no supplier". So the precondition the app demands is that every part must have a supplier recorded; nothing else was changed — the ticket's status is still Draft, both parts and the $437.50 total are untouched (screenshot of the error state captured).

steps.summary: I edited both parts on RD-1017 via their Edit actions: Part "fwrd71-n3 RD Part A" set Supplier "Acme Supplies" (cost left 150, markup 25, price $187.50) and Part "fwrd71-n3 RD Part B" set Supplier "Acme Supplies" (cost left 200, markup 25, price $250.00); total stayed $437.50. I then clicked "Mark Ready" — no error appeared (the old role="alert" error region is now empty) and the page's Status field reads "Ready", with the available actions switching from "Mark Ready" to "Mark Draft"/"Mark Closed". No separate confirmation toast/text was present; the confirmation is the status label itself, verified in the live DOM snapshot and screenshot.

steps.summary: On RD-1017 I deleted both parts via their Delete actions, each time confirming the in-page "Confirm" dialog with "Delete part"; after each deletion the list refreshed and the Parts section now reads "No parts on this ticket yet." I then clicked "Archive ticket" — it succeeded on the first attempt with no error or precondition message, and the action switched to "Unarchive ticket" (the detail page shows Status "Ready" plus a separate "Archived" badge). On the tickets list, searching RD-1017 with archived hidden returns "No tickets match the current filters.", while ticking "Show archived" reveals the row "RD-1017 | fwrd71-n3 RD Bench Ticket Archived | Bench Customer | Ready | 0 | 2026-09-17". So nothing further was demanded to archive it.
